about: Hand-curated registry of the property keys the Forge bridge emits on tokens, action options and records. Each component of a token is encoded as (key embedding, value repr); the key embedding is the frozen text embedding of `description`. Counter keys are expanded from counter_keys.json (generated from Forge by scripts/gen_counter_keys.py). tests/test_keys.py fails when the bridge emits a key that is not here. Layout (schema 9): `identity` and `ref` keys sit at the top level of a token next to `type`, `zone` and `edges`; every other key (number/flag/string/string_list) is nested under the token's `components` object, which is omitted when empty, and flags appear only when true. magicnet.bridge.Schema.isTopLevel implements this split and tests/test_schema.py checks it against this file. Action options and the record envelope are not tokens and stay flat.

value_kinds.string: short string; embed the value with the catalog's text embedder (POST /strings/embed)
value_kinds.string_list: list of short strings; embed each and pool
value_kinds.ref: names or points at another object/player; top-level (not under components); should become an edge
value_kinds.identity: join key / token identity, not a component; top-level; never encoded as (key, value)

role_java_exprs_about: EventTokenizer.card/player/entity/zone write the role name itself (t.p(role, ...)); tests/test_keys.py checks every literal role passed to them is a registered key.
record_fields_about: Serializer's decision-record envelope. Not token components, except kind/turn/phase which are registered keys (turn and phase duplicate the global token).
